summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow to create executable PLAN.md files for CipherBox Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability), then run the execute-phase workflow to implement all resulting plans via wave-based parallel worktree execution.
summary.outcome: Planning produced 13 plans across 7 waves (decision coverage 17/17, plan-checker passed) after two user-driven scope expansions (Rust engine twin, desktop FUSE live-wiring). Execution completed and gated 12/13 plans (waves 1-6 all green), fixed a real product bug the new depth-3 e2e gate uncovered (decrypt-before-dirtiness-check ordering in both TS/Rust engines) and a critical missing `refresh_sent_shares` wiring gap on the desktop mount; only Wave 7's human sign-off for the real-mount desktop-e2e acceptance run remains.

repo: GSD decision-coverage parser only accepts three D-NN bullet formats (`- **D-NN:**`, `- **D-NN — title**`, `- **D-NN: Title.**`); a single malformed bullet anywhere in CONTEXT.md fails the whole gate silently with '0/N covered'.

Worktree executors must scope `cargo fmt`/`clippy` to `-p <package>`, not workspace-wide — an unscoped `cargo fmt --all` leaves large out-of-scope reformatting drift uncommitted in the worktree, which blocks the merge helper with `worktree_dirty`.
GSD's commit helper can report `commit_failed` on slow lint-staged runs even though the commit landed — always verify via `git log`, never blind-retry.
`gsd_run loop render-hooks plan:pre --raw` emits invalid JSON (literal newlines in fragments); read the hooks file directly instead of parsing the raw output.

`state.planned-phase` / similar STATE.md update tools can silently no-op (`updated: []`) if STATE.md's anchor fields don't match the expected format — must verify with a follow-up read, not trust the echoed success.

sdk-e2e's vitest config has no dotenv loader and its `test` script is bare `vitest run` — `.env` (incl. `SDK_E2E_SECRET`) must be sourced into the shell manually before running locally, or the harness silently falls back to a default secret and login 401s.

After changing sdk-core mid-phase, the `sdk` package's consumer dist must be rebuilt too — running vitest against a stale cross-package dist produces false failures indistinguishable from real regressions.

CipherBox delete is a soft-delete (item moves to the owner's private recycle bin, keys re-sealed under the bin plane) — structurally identical to a cross-folder move, which is why deletes (not just renames) trigger scope-exit rotation.
The scope-exit rotation gate only fires on cross-folder rename (`parent != newparent`); same-folder renames are explicitly excluded since the node never leaves scope.

Desktop FUSE mount (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs`) never called `CipherBoxFS::refresh_sent_shares`, so `sent_shares` stayed non-authoritative — combined with the phase's new fail-closed gate, this caused every real-mount delete/rename to EIO.

code.finding: collectDirtyFrontier/resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope unconditionally AEAD-decrypted a child's sealed ref with the parent's current key before checking plaintext generation for dirtiness — a genuinely dirty edge whose parent also rotated always threw CryptoError; fix reorders the plaintext generation check before any decrypt attempt.
rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally stubbed with Err (fail-closed EIO); Plan 09 wired it to a new production FuseRotationDeps adapter.
Scope-exit gate only invoked when parent != newparent, confirming same-folder renames never rotate.
unlink_shared_scope_exit_fails_closed_until_rotation_wired test needed inversion once live-wiring landed; required an in-process mock IPNS server built to avoid fabricating a false pass.

workflow: When running parallel worktree waves, dispatch one Agent call per message rather than batching simultaneous `git worktree add` calls — concurrent creation races on `.git/config.lock`.

Running a single plan as a synchronous 'canary' before fanning out a full wave is a reasonable risk-reduction tactic for worktree-merge mechanics, but must be explicitly flagged to the user since it looks like under-parallelizing.

When a gate the phase specifically built (like an anti-vacuous e2e fixture) fails, treat it as a signal to investigate for a genuine product bug rather than assuming a fixture/env issue — spawn a scientific-method debugging subagent that is explicitly forbidden from patching the test to pass.

Post-merge integration gates should be run centrally by the orchestrator (not per-worktree) after merging concurrent plans, since cross-plan compile/behavior interactions only surface once both diffs are combined.

friction: Decision-coverage gate blocked on pre-existing D-09/D-10 bullets with a period-before-`**` format, requiring a parser deep-dive to diagnose
render-hooks --raw JSON output was unparseable due to literal newlines
state.planned-phase tool silently no-op'd, requiring manual STATE.md edits
Worktree merge blocked by unscoped cargo fmt drift in plan 03's worktree
Stale cross-package dist caused 3 false test failures after Wave 3 merge, requiring rebuild-and-recheck
sdk-e2e login 401'd due to missing .env sourcing, requiring root-cause tracing through vitest config
Stale rust-analyzer diagnostics (macros.rs, fs.rs NodeKind) triggered unnecessary investigation before being dismissed as false positives
User challenged the orchestrator for only running 1 of 4 Wave 1 plans concurrently; orchestrator had to admit it was an unflagged canary run
Mid-planning scope crept twice (Rust engine twin, then FUSE live-wiring), each requiring CONTEXT/ROADMAP/VALIDATION/todo rework and re-research
Plan 13's checkpoint agent surfaced a critical unwired refresh_sent_shares gap mid-execution, forcing an unplanned fix before the human sign-off could even be meaningfully requested
